To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
isolated microsporocytes of Trillium erectum synthesize RNA and protein in a pattern that reflects the cytological changes of meiosis and that part of the RNA is messenger-like.

the microsporocytes of Trillium erectum, in the course of meiosis, synthesize RNA and protein at a rate that increases during pachytenu and diplotene and that this increase in synthesis is accompanied by a corresponding increase in the rate of transcription.

(1) the capacity of microsporocytes of Trillium to synthesize protein is induced during pachytence and diplotene; (2) the synthesis of RNA is also induced during these stages; (3) part of the RNA is messenger-like; (4) the induction of RNA and protein synthesis is a function of the stage of meiosis at the time of isolation; and (5) the induction of synthesis is not solely the result of low temperature.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the molecular mechanisms of meiosis.
the problem of how the information stored in the genome is translated into the sequence of morphogenetic events that constitute the process of meiosis.
the problem of the relationship between the structure of the chromosome and the function of genes in the cell nucleus.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the meiotic sequence is a function of the genome and is not a function of the cytoplasm, as is the case in the mitotic cycle.

the meiotic sequence is not merely a passive consequence of chromosome contraction but is a highly ordered series of reactions which are under the control of a set of genes which have been conserved in evolution.
the events associated with meiosis are a consequence of gene transcriptions which are induced by some as yet undefined mechanism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the meiotic sequence in Trillium, and probably other species, is not a passive response to temperature but is an integrated set of events which can be initiated in isolated cells by the action of genes which are transcribed during pachyteneri and diplotene.
the microsporocyte, like the somatic cell, can be induced to perform a variety of syntheses.
the meiotic process is a complex series of gene transcriptions, each of which is essential to the completion of the meiotic sequence.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the meiotic sequence is an expression of the genome.
meiotic events are accompanied by a set transcriptional activity.
meiosis is not merely a process of DNA segregation but is also a process of information retrieval and expression.
